constructions.label: すると: then, and (the next development or discovery after an event)
その結果: as a result (a causal result of what precedes)
そこで: so, therefore (a deliberate step chosen in response to the situation)
ところが: however (what happened ran against the expectation just set up)
ところで: by the way (moving to a new topic)
つまり: in other words (restating or summing up what was said)
また: also (adding a further, separate point)
あるいは: or (one of two alternatives)
かえって: if anything, on the contrary (an outcome opposite to the intention)
やはり: as expected, after all (the outcome or conclusion confirms what was usual or expected)
〜一方で: while, on the other hand (two sides that are both true)
〜代わりに: instead of (one thing replaces another)
なぜなら〜からだ: this is because (a reason sentence closed by からだ／からである)
そのため: for this reason (a consequence of what was just said)
である／だ: plain written style, kept throughout one text
です／ます: polite style, kept throughout one text
Passive in a narrative: the narrator is affected by someone else's action
Causative in a narrative: the narrator makes or has someone do something
〜てあげた: the narrator did a favour for someone
〜てもらった: the narrator received a favour from someone (who is marked with に)
〜ていた: reports a state as found, without saying how or why it arose
〜てあった: a state, foregrounding that someone deliberately arranged it
〜ておいた: the preparer's own action done in advance (the doer is the subject)

relationships.label: What follows in a narrative: the next event (すると), an outcome (その結果) or a deliberate response (そこで)
Against the expectation (ところが) versus a new topic (ところで)
Restating (つまり), adding (また) or giving an alternative (あるいは) in a passage
An outcome opposite to the intention (かえって) versus one that confirms what was expected (やはり)
Two sides that are both true (一方で) versus replacement (代わりに), decided by the rest of the passage
Matching the opening of a sentence to its ending and to the passage: なぜなら〜からだ versus そのため
Keeping one style through a text: plain である／だ versus polite です／ます
Passive versus causative, decided by who acts and how the narrator feels later in the passage
Who did the favour: 〜てあげた versus 〜てもらった, decided by roles and thanks later in the passage
A state as found (〜ていた), a state presented as deliberately arranged (〜てあった) or the preparer's own advance action (〜ておいた), decided by the rest of the passage

exercises.evidence: The sentence before reports a trial (prices cut for the last hour before closing); the blank's sentence reports changes nobody chose (more evening customers, half the waste).
exercises.explanation: I run a small bakery in front of the station. Mornings are always busy, but after midday hardly any customers came, and unsold bread had to be thrown away every day. Last month, as a trial, I lowered the bread prices for just the last hour before closing. As a result, more customers came in the evening, and the bread we throw away was halved. options.rationale: Fits: more customers and less waste are outcomes produced by the trial price cut.

options.label: そこで
options.rationale: Doesn't fit this passage: そこで introduces a step someone deliberately takes to deal with a situation; customers increasing and waste falling are not steps anyone chose.

additionalCorrectOptions.rationale: Also correct: すると simply presents the changes as what came after the trial, the next development.
